units.2 Chronicles 20:5: Jehoshaphat stood in the assembly of Judah in Jerusalem, in the Lord’s house before the new courtyard.
units.2 Chronicles 20:6: He said, “Lord, God of our fathers, art Thou not God in heaven? Thou rulest over all the kingdoms of the nations. In Thy hand is mighty strength, and no one can resist Thee.
units.2 Chronicles 20:7: Was it not Thou, O Lord, who didst destroy this land’s inhabitants before Thy people Israel and didst give it for ever to the descendants of Abraham, Thy beloved?
units.2 Chronicles 20:8: They dwelt in it and built a sanctuary in it for Thy name, saying,
units.2 Chronicles 20:9: ‘If calamities come upon us—sword, judgment, death, famine—we will stand before this house and before Thee, for Thy name is upon this house. We will cry to Thee from affliction, and Thou wilt hear and save.’
units.2 Chronicles 20:10: Now behold the sons of Ammon and Moab and Mount Seir, through whom Thou didst not let Israel pass when they came out from Egypt’s land. They turned aside from them and did not destroy them.
units.2 Chronicles 20:11: Now behold: they are attempting to come out against us and expel us from our inheritance, which Thou didst give us.
units.2 Chronicles 20:12: O Lord our God, wilt Thou not judge among them? For we have no strength to withstand this great multitude that has come against us, and we do not know what we should do to them: but our eyes are upon Thee.”
units.2 Chronicles 20:14: The Spirit of the Lord came upon Oziel son of Zacharias, of the sons of Banaias, of the sons of Eleel, of Manthanias the Levite, from Asaph’s sons, in the assembly.
units.2 Chronicles 20:15: He said, “Listen, all Judah, inhabitants of Jerusalem, and King Jehoshaphat! Thus says the Lord to you yourselves: Do not fear or be terrified before this great crowd, because the battle array belongs to God, not to you.
units.2 Chronicles 20:16: Tomorrow go down against them. Behold, they are coming up by the ascent of Asas. You will find them at the edge of the river of the wilderness of Jeriel.
units.2 Chronicles 20:17: You will not have to wage war. Understand these things and see the Lord’s salvation with you, Judah and Jerusalem. Do not fear or be terrified about going out tomorrow to meet them, and the Lord will be with you.”
units.Deuteronomy 31:9: And Moses wrote the words of this law in a book, and gave it unto the priests, the sons of Levi, who bear the ark of the covenant of the Lord, and unto the elders of the sons of Israel.

units.Joshua 9:2a: Then Joshua built an altar to the Lord, the God of Israel, on Mount Ebal,
units.Joshua 9:2b: as Moses, the servant of the Lord, commanded the sons of Israel, as written in Moses’ law: an altar of whole stones on which no iron had been applied. He offered whole burnt offerings to the Lord there and a sacrifice of well-being.
units.Joshua 9:2c: Joshua wrote on the stones the second law, Moses’ law, which he wrote before the sons of Israel.
units.Joshua 9:2d: All Israel, their elders, judges, and scribes passed on either side opposite the ark. The priests and Levites carried the ark of the covenant of the Lord. Resident alien and native alike were there, half near Mount Gerizim and half near Mount Ebal, as Moses, the servant of the Lord, had first commanded the blessing of the people.
units.Joshua 9:2e: After this Joshua read all the words of this law, the blessings and the curses, according to everything written in Moses’ law.
units.Joshua 9:2f: There was not a word of everything Moses commanded Joshua that Joshua did not read in the hearing of the whole assembly of the sons of Israel: the men, women, children, and resident aliens travelling with Israel.
units.2 Chronicles 26:1: All the people of the land took Uzziah, who was sixteen years old, and made him king in place of his father Amaziah.
units.2 Chronicles 26:2: He built Ailath; he restored it to Judah after the king fell asleep with his fathers.
units.2 Chronicles 26:3: Uzziah became king at sixteen years of age, and he reigned fifty-two years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Chalia from Jerusalem.
units.2 Chronicles 26:4: He did what was right before the Lord, according to everything his father Amaziah had done.
units.2 Chronicles 26:5: He sought the Lord in the days of Zacharias, who understood the fear of the Lord. In his days he sought the Lord, and the Lord made him prosper.
units.2 Chronicles 26:6: He went out and fought the foreigners. He pulled down Geth’s walls, Jabne’s walls, and Azotus’s walls, and built cities of Azotus and among the foreigners.
units.2 Chronicles 26:7: The Lord strengthened him against the foreigners, against the Arabs living on the rock, and against the Minaeans.
units.2 Chronicles 26:8: The Minaeans gave gifts to Uzziah, and his name reached as far as Egypt’s entrance, because he grew exceedingly strong.
units.2 Chronicles 26:9: Uzziah built towers in Jerusalem, at the Corner Gate, the Ravine Gate, and at the corners, and grew strong.
units.2 Chronicles 26:11: Uzziah had forces that waged war and went out to battle array by number. Their number was recorded by Iiel the scribe and Maasaias the judge under Ananias, the king’s deputy.
units.2 Chronicles 26:12: The total number of ancestral rulers mighty for war was two thousand six hundred.
units.2 Chronicles 26:13: With them was a fighting force of three hundred seven thousand five hundred, waging war with mighty strength to help the king against his adversaries.
units.2 Chronicles 26:14: Uzziah prepared for them, for the whole force, large shields, spears, helmets, breastplates, bows, and slings for stones.
units.2 Chronicles 26:15: In Jerusalem he made machines devised by a designer to stand on the towers and corners for shooting missiles and large stones. Their construction was heard of far away, for he was wonderfully helped until he grew strong.
units.Ecclesiastes 1:12: I, Ecclesiastes, became king over Israel in Jerusalem.
units.Ecclesiastes 1:13: I set my heart to seek out and examine by wisdom everything that happens beneath heaven, for God gave human beings a grievous distraction to be distracted by.
units.Ecclesiastes 1:14: I saw all the works done beneath the sun, and behold, everything is futility and resolve of spirit.
units.Ecclesiastes 1:15: What is twisted cannot be put in order, and what is lacking cannot be counted.
units.Ecclesiastes 1:16: I spoke in my heart, saying: Behold, I became great and added wisdom beyond everyone who was in Jerusalem before me, and my heart saw much—wisdom and knowledge.
units.Ecclesiastes 1:17: I set my heart to know wisdom and knowledge; I came to know comparisons and understanding, for this too is resolve of spirit.
units.Ecclesiastes 1:18: For in much wisdom is much knowledge, and whoever increases knowledge will increase pain.
units.Ecclesiastes 2:1: I said in my heart: Come now, I will test you with gladness; experience good. But behold, this too was futility.
units.Ecclesiastes 2:2: Of laughter I said, “Delirium!” And to gladness, “What are you doing?”
units.Ecclesiastes 2:3: I examined in my heart how to draw my flesh toward wine—while my heart guided me with wisdom—and how to take hold of folly, until I might see what good human beings should do beneath the sun during the numbered days of their lives.
units.Ecclesiastes 2:4: I enlarged my work; I built houses for myself and planted vineyards for myself,
units.Ecclesiastes 2:5: I made gardens and parks for myself and planted in them every kind of fruit tree.
units.Ecclesiastes 2:6: I made pools of water for myself to irrigate from them a woodland sprouting trees.
units.Ecclesiastes 2:7: I acquired male and female slaves, and I had slaves born in my house. I also had a great possession of herds and flocks, beyond everyone who was before me in Jerusalem.
units.Ecclesiastes 2:8: I also gathered silver and gold for myself, and the riches of kings and regions. I provided male and female singers for myself, and human delights—a male cupbearer and female cupbearers.
units.Ecclesiastes 2:9: I grew great and surpassed everyone who was before me in Jerusalem; my wisdom also remained with me.
units.Ecclesiastes 2:10: Whatever my eyes asked for, I did not withhold from them. I did not keep my heart from any gladness, for my heart rejoiced in all my toil, and this was my portion from all my toil.
units.Ecclesiastes 2:11: Then I looked upon all my works that my hands had done and the toil with which I had labored to do them, and behold, everything was futility and resolve of spirit, with no surplus beneath the sun.
units.2 Chronicles 29:18: They went inside to King Hezekiah and said, “We have purified everything in the Lord’s house: the altar of burnt offering and its articles, and the table of presentation and its articles.
units.2 Chronicles 29:19: All the articles King Ahaz defiled in his reign through his apostasy we have prepared and purified. Behold, they are before the Lord’s altar.”
units.2 Chronicles 29:21: He brought up seven calves, seven rams, seven lambs, and seven male goats for sin, for the kingdom, the holy places, and Israel. He told Aaron’s sons, the priests, to go up onto the Lord’s altar.
units.2 Chronicles 29:22: They sacrificed the calves, and the priests received the blood and poured it onto the altar. They sacrificed the rams and poured the blood onto the altar. They sacrificed the lambs and poured the blood around the altar.
units.2 Chronicles 29:23: They brought the male goats for sin before the king and the assembly, and they laid their hands on them.
units.2 Chronicles 29:24: The priests sacrificed them and made propitiation with their blood at the altar, and made propitiation for all Israel, because the king had said, “The burnt offering and the offerings for sin are for all Israel.”
units.2 Kings 23:1: The king sent and gathered to himself all the elders of Judah and Jerusalem.
units.2 Kings 23:2: The king went up to the Lord’s house, with every man of Judah and all who inhabited Jerusalem, the priests, the prophets, and all the people, from small to great. He read in their hearing all the words of the covenant book found in the Lord’s house.
units.2 Kings 23:3: The king stood beside the pillar and made a covenant before the Lord: to follow the Lord and keep His commandments, testimonies, and ordinances with the whole heart and whole soul, upholding the words of this covenant, the things written in this book. All the people stood in the covenant.
units.2 Chronicles 32:20: King Hezekiah and Isaiah son of Amoz the prophet prayed about these things and cried out to heaven.
units.2 Chronicles 32:21: The Lord sent an angel, and he wiped out every mighty warrior, ruler, and commander in the camp of the king of Assyria. The king returned to his land with shame of face. He entered the house of his god, and some who had come from his own body struck him down with the sword.
units.2 Chronicles 32:22: The Lord saved Hezekiah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem from the hand of Sennacherib king of Assyria and from everyone’s hand, and He gave them rest all around.
units.2 Chronicles 32:24: In those days Hezekiah became ill to the point of death. He prayed to the Lord, and He listened to him and gave him a sign.
units.2 Chronicles 32:25: Hezekiah did not repay according to the recompense He had given him, but his heart was lifted up. Wrath came upon him and upon Judah and Jerusalem.
units.2 Chronicles 32:26: Hezekiah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem humbled themselves from the height of his heart, and the Lord’s wrath did not come upon them in Hezekiah’s days.
units.2 Chronicles 32:27: Hezekiah had exceedingly great wealth and glory. He made himself treasuries for silver, gold, precious stones, and spices, and armories, and places for desirable articles,
units.2 Chronicles 32:29: and cities that he built for himself, and a great stock of sheep and cattle, because the Lord gave him exceedingly many possessions.
units.2 Chronicles 32:30: Hezekiah himself blocked the upper outlet of the water of Gihon and directed the waters downward toward the southwest of the City of David. Hezekiah prospered in all his works.

units.Psalms 75:4: There He crushed the bows’ powers, weapon and sword and war. Diapsalma.
units.Psalms 75:5: Thou givest light wondrously from everlasting mountains.
units.Psalms 75:6: All those without understanding in heart were troubled; they slept their sleep, and all the men of wealth found nothing with their hands.
units.Psalms 75:7: At Thy rebuke, God of Jacob, those mounted on horses grew drowsy.
units.Psalms 75:8: Thou art fearsome, and who will withstand Thee? From that time is Thy wrath.
units.Psalms 75:9: From heaven Thou didst cause judgment to be heard; the earth feared and grew quiet,
units.Psalms 75:10: when God arose for judgment, to save all the earth’s meek. Diapsalma.
units.Psalms 75:11: For human thought will acknowledge Thee, and the remainder of thought will keep a feast for Thee.
units.Psalms 75:12: Make vows and repay the Lord your God; all around Him will bring gifts
units.Psalms 75:13: to the Fearsome One, who takes away rulers’ spirits, who is fearsome among the earth’s kings.

reread_versions.relationship: women and children explicitly included in the assembly before the Lord
reread_versions.rationale: Chronicles explicitly includes children and women as all Judah stands before the Lord; Deuteronomy calls for Israel to appear before Him and commands the gathering of men, women, children and the sojourner. The correspondence concerns the assembly's inclusive composition; Chronicles' crisis prayer is not identified as the prescribed festival reading.

reread_versions.relationship: women and children present within the whole assembled people
reread_versions.rationale: Chronicles names the children and women standing with all Judah; the native Joshua continuation unit names women and children among the whole assembly hearing the law. Both explicitly include these family members, while the prayer assembly and law reading remain distinct events and Joshua's original 9:2f reference is preserved.

reread_versions.relationship: royal agricultural works combining water provision, cultivated land and livestock
reread_versions.rationale: Uzziah's works include cisterns, herds and vinedressers, with his love of farming stated; the royal speaker in Ecclesiastes describes vineyards, gardens, water pools and great herds and flocks. The shared combination gives a particular parallel in royal agriculture, without equating the rulers or the cisterns for herds with the pools used to irrigate trees.

reread_versions.relationship: gifts brought to the Lord after His victory over hostile power
reread_versions.rationale: Chronicles places gifts to the Lord at Jerusalem after the defeat of Assyria and Jerusalem's deliverance; Psalm 75, explicitly titled concerning the Assyrian, moves from God's defeat of weapons at Zion to gifts brought to the Lord who overawes rulers. The link concerns the gifts to God after divine victory, not a claim that the psalm names Hezekiah or records the separate presents to him.

reread_versions.rationale: Hezekiah's possessions include provision for grain, oil and wine and places for animals and flocks; David's estate roster separately names storehouses, wine and oil stores, cattle and sheep. The detailed combination connects the management of royal agricultural resources while preserving the different rulers, personnel and types of facilities.

case.source_text: King Hezekiah rose early, gathered the city’s rulers, and went up to the Lord’s house.
case.reason: The source and a newly checked reform-assembly candidate were read in full with context. The comparison gives only a general king-and-leaders procession to the Lord's house; it does not establish a sufficiently particular new connection for Hezekiah's early rising and restoration-sacrifice transition. The source remains pending with zero completion credit.

case.source_text: King Hezekiah rose early, gathered the city’s rulers, and went up to the Lord’s house.
case.reason: Hezekiah gathers city rulers and goes up early before restoration sacrifices; Kings describes the gathering of elders and a procession for a covenant-book reading. The common royal assembly pattern was judged too general for a retained additional relationship here; no identification of the events is made.

target_units.text: The king sent and gathered to himself all the elders of Judah and Jerusalem.

The king went up to the Lord’s house, with every man of Judah and all who inhabited Jerusalem, the priests, the prophets, and all the people, from small to great. He read in their hearing all the words of the covenant book found in the Lord’s house.

The king stood beside the pillar and made a covenant before the Lord: to follow the Lord and keep His commandments, testimonies, and ordinances with the whole heart and whole soul, upholding the words of this covenant, the things written in this book. All the people stood in the covenant.
